per_window.ps-ns: Not resolved for any wild-type state. No row gives per-residue order parameters for oxidised Cu(II) azurin (J1, search_insufficient). The RelaxDB source paper's abstract (copper azurin, oxidation state not stated) reports fast internal motion in the loop 103-108 and the turn 74-77 and an average S2 of 0.85 ± 0.05 elsewhere, including the copper site (J37, C-r1, unresolved). Reduced Cu(I) azurin has only an abstract that calls H117 and the hydrophobic patch mobile and N47-V49 relatively rigid (J17, r16, r17). The homologous CuA domain is rigid on this scale in apo and holo forms (r47, r48, not judged).
per_window.us-ms: Reference Cu(II): not measured (J2). Reduced Cu(I) at pH about 5, 50 mM phosphate: two slow processes seen by 15N CPMG at three fields, one around H35 (D11, G37, G88-G90; kA 11.7 ± 2.4 s-1, 0.39 ± 0.07% at 44.8 °C; J12, r9), tied by the authors to H35 protonation and a peptide flip, and one in the copper loops (N47, W48, F111-T113, G116, H117, L120, K122; kA 4.1 ± 0.1 s-1, 0.45 ± 0.02%; J13, r10); residues in between sense both (J14, r11); per-residue kA 0.44-9.55 s-1 at 35.4 °C (J15, r12); 29 named amides pass across 25.7-44.8 °C (J16, r13-r15). Apo at 298 K, pH 7.0: 17 amides around the metal site broadened out by intermediate exchange (J18, r44), dispersion at M44, I87 and two more regions (J19, r45), none at T61 (J20, r46); high-pH 1H broadening of histidines, abstract only (J22). Homolog apo CuA shows the same pattern (J36). The RelaxDB source paper's abstract adds exchange broadening around H35 in copper azurin of unstated oxidation state, with the rate placed in the slower-than-ms window (J38).
per_window.slower_than_ms: Not measured for the oxidised wild type as such (J3). The RelaxDB source paper (abstract only) gives an average exchange rate of 45 ± 6 s-1 at 41 °C by exchange spectroscopy for the residues around H35, attributed to H35 protonation/deprotonation, and says the pH 5.5 and pH 9.0 crystal conformations coexist in solution and interconvert slowly (J38, C-r2, unresolved; oxidation state not stated). The Cu(I) forward rates of 4-12 s-1 are reported within the CPMG analysis and stay in the us-ms window. Single-molecule ET-rate fluctuations over tens to hundreds of seconds (J33) are electron-transfer kinetics, not conformational.
per_window.undetermined: Static and indirect items, none counted as exchange: oxidised crystals at two pH values with a P36-G37 flip (J4, abstract); DEPC histidine accessibility (J5); femtosecond coherences and charge transfer (J6, photophysics); holo fluorescence heterogeneity (J7, abstract); forced unfolding by steered MD and AFM (J8, J9, J26, J27); ionic-liquid and electrode studies (J10, J11); two apo crystal forms (J21, abstract); W48 phosphorescence and acrylamide quenching in apo and Cd forms (J23, J24, J29); 3 μs MD of apo and Zn azurin with loop fluctuation and water entry (J25, J30, md_only); Fe-, Zn-, Co- and Ni-substituted crystals (J28, J31, J32, J40); temperature-jump slow phase of the azurin/cytochrome c551 mixture assigned to H35 (J39, C-r3, abstract); Ru- and Re-labelled constructs (J34, J35, ET and photophysics). protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Copper-free wild-type azurin (298 K, pH 7.0, 100 mM phosphate, 2 mM DTT) does show microsecond-millisecond exchange around the metal site: 17 amides (A1-C3, G9-D11, N18, H35-L39, G45, H46, G88-E91) are broadened out by intermediate exchange and CPMG dispersion appears at M44, I87 and neighbouring regions, but no rate or population is reported; for the copper-bound forms, no exchange measurement exists for oxidised Cu(II) azurin, and only reduced Cu(I) azurin has rates (minor states of 0.39% and 0.45% at 44.8 °C, pH about 5). The RelaxDB source paper (doi:10.1021/bi990624l, abstract only, oxidation state not stated) adds slow exchange around H35 at 45 ± 6 s-1 (41 °C), read by the authors as interconversion of the pH 5.5 and pH 9.0 crystal conformations in solution (J38, unresolved).
open_conflicts: Not a conflict but a state contrast: apo-azurin loses 17 amides to intermediate exchange, while the authors cite a full Cu(I) HSQC (all non-proline residues but A1); the apo (pH 7.0, 100 mM phosphate, DTT) and Cu(I) (pH about 5, 50 mM phosphate) samples also differ in pH and buffer, so metal state and pH are confounded.
Residue 116: the CPMG paper's Table 2 prints 'Cys 116' while the entry sequence has G116; the judgments follow the sequence (row AZURIN-r10 still prints C116).

H35 process rate: the 1999 RelaxDB source abstract gives an average exchange rate of 45 ± 6 s-1 at 41 °C from exchange spectroscopy (C-r2, J38, oxidation state and pH not stated), whereas the 2003 Cu(I) CPMG fit at 44.8 °C gives kA 11.7 ± 2.4 s-1 with a 0.39% minor state (r9, J12), which implies a total exchange rate in the thousands per second; the two may be different states, pH values or models, and only the 2003 paper was read in full.
questions_for_gina: Which azurin sample is the RelaxDB entry: oxidised Cu(II), reduced Cu(I), or apo? The RelaxDB source paper (doi:10.1021/bi990624l) was read only as an abstract, which does not state the oxidation state; the missing-peak annotations would fit paramagnetic Cu(II) broadening or the apo intermediate exchange (BMRB 18254, apo, pH 7.0) equally well.

Should the H35 process count as conformational exchange, given that the 1999 source calls it H35 protonation/deprotonation interconverting the pH 5.5 and 9.0 crystal conformations at 45 ± 6 s-1 (41 °C), and the 2003 Cu(I) CPMG paper links its minor population to the protonated fraction of H35?
protein_summary.buffer_note: Every NMR dynamics sample is in phosphate: 50 mM, pH about 5 for Cu(I) CPMG (r9-r15) and 100 mM, pH 7.0 with 2 mM DTT for apo (r44-r46); no row tests a phosphate effect or a buffer change. The apo protein was made by KCN dialysis. Phosphorescence work (r1-r43) uses 2 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.5 at 20 °C with Cd(II) or Zn(II) standing in for copper. The RelaxDB source paper (C-r1, C-r2) is abstract-only: no pH, buffer or oxidation state, 41 °C for the exchange-spectroscopy rate. Row-id shorthand: A-rN = AZURIN-AZURIN_20261020003349-rN, B-rN = AZURIN-AZURIN_20261020005254-rN, C-rN = AZURIN-AZURIN_20261020143153-rN. Second reads of the C rows flagged nothing (Codex left nine and Claude five unverified).
